status: PROPOSAL — staged, not live. Authored by Aevi (PO) as the SNG-263 pilot. CCode folds into the ability records once the schema is locked; nothing here writes to reach_dark_light.json.
note: SNG-263 pilot: 12 blazeborn crafts given a mechanical body DERIVED FROM their existing rank prose (tree[].grants) and bounded by their existing tree[].cannot. The text is the spec — every axis and every rank increment below is traceable to a line the content already committed to. Damage model per §11: TOTAL = dice(tier,rank) + scaling(level, attribute, uses) − soak(target); the craft authors its DICE and its OPERATIVE AXIS only. Ladder per §10: T-I 1d6 (+1 at r2, +2 at r3), T-II 2d6, T-III 3d6+2, T-IV/V dice + a SPECIAL. A rank may spend its increment on a DIFFERENT axis when its own prose names one — that is the point of the pilot.

conventions.operativeAxis: What this craft actually does — the dimension its magnitudes and its intensity scaling apply to. Never assume damage.
conventions.rankDeltas: What r1→r2→r3 CHANGES, and on which axis, traceable to that rank's own grants line.
conventions.intensity: conserve ≈ half / surge ≈ double ON THE OPERATIVE AXIS, stated in this craft's own language. Some crafts refuse a mode — that is authored, not an omission.
conventions.bounds: Mechanical limits taken from tree[].cannot — these are intent, not decoration.

crafts.designNote: The pilot's proof that intensity must be PER-CRAFT and audited: a blanket ×0.5/×2 would have silently created a 'conserved last light,' which the craft's own cannot-text forbids. Erik's audit-each-craft instruction, vindicated by the first capstone it touched.

pilotFindings: The prose carried the mechanics. Every axis and every rank increment above is traceable to a line already in tree[].grants — nothing was invented. The authoring job is TRANSCRIPTION plus arithmetic, not invention.

Only 4 of 12 blazeborn crafts are damage-carrying (kindle, radiance, the_revealing_burn, the_last_light). The other 8 needed healing, soak, area, range, duration, targets, materials, persistence, and bind-strength. A damage-only schema would have failed 2/3 of a single tradition.

Rank increments landed on a NON-damage axis more often than on damage: kindle r3 buys range+persistence, radiance r2 buys area, lightsense r3 buys range, the_line_of_light r3 buys companions. The §10 rule (a rank spends on the axis its own prose names) is not an edge case — it is the common case.

the_last_light REFUSES both intensity modes on the authority of its own cannot-text ('it cannot be half-given'). A blanket conserve/surge multiplier would have invented a mode the fiction forbids. This is the single clearest vindication of Erik's audit-every-craft instruction.
the_blaze_wall cannot be authored at all without §11 Gap 2 (soak/armor). Its whole body is a barrier value. Confirms the soak layer is a blocker, not a nice-to-have.

the_revealing_burn r2 is already an IDENTITY ATTACK in the existing prose ('what is false in a PERSON — an assumed shape, a worn name'). SNG-258 §4e (alignment/experience can be assailed) is not a new system to invent — the catalog already reaches for it, and this craft is its first concrete instance.

T-IV/V 'special' has a clear register from the prose: the craft gains a KIND it did not have (identity-attack; total expenditure with total self-cost), not a bigger number. That answers Erik's open question without needing worked examples from him — though his sign-off on the register is still wanted.
openForErik: Sign off the dice ladder as applied here (T-I 1d6 / T-II 2d6 / T-III 3d6+2 / T-IV 4d6+2 / T-V 5d6+4).
The scaling term's strength (§11): how much better should a master's kindle be than a novice's kindle?
Whether 'REFUSED' is the right authored value for an intensity mode a craft's fiction forbids, or whether it should read as something else in the UI.
